sections.title: EC2 Fundamentals: What It Is, Sizing Options and User Data
keyTopics: EC2 as Infrastructure as a Service
Renting VMs, EBS, ELB, ASG roles
Security group as firewall rule set
User Data runs once as root
sections.objective: Explain what EC2 provides, list the sizing/configuration choices at launch, and describe what an EC2 User Data script does and when it runs.

sections.title: EC2 Instance Types: Naming Convention and Families
keyTopics: Instance sizing table (vCPU, memory, network, EBS)
sections.objective: Choose the appropriate EC2 instance family (general purpose, compute, memory, storage optimized) for a given workload and decode instance names such as m5.2xlarge.

sections.title: Security Groups and Classic Ports
keyTopics: Rules by IP range or security group
Security groups as stateful firewall outside EC2
sections.objective: Apply security group rules to control ports, IP ranges and traffic direction, reference other security groups, and diagnose connectivity failures using the classic port numbers.

sections.title: Connecting to EC2 Instances: SSH, Putty and EC2 Instance Connect
keyTopics: SSH client by OS (Mac, Linux, Windows)
sections.objective: Select the right connection method for a given client OS and explain how EC2 Instance Connect works without a downloaded key file.

sections.title: EC2 Purchasing Options and Price Comparison
keyTopics: Capacity Reservations in a specific AZ
sections.objective: Choose the cost-optimal EC2 purchasing option for a workload's duration, predictability, fault tolerance and licensing/compliance constraints, and distinguish Dedicated Hosts from Dedicated Instances and Capacity Reservations.

sections.title: Spot Instances: Requests, Termination and Spot Fleets
keyTopics: Max spot price vs current spot price
sections.objective: Explain how Spot requests are interrupted and terminated, and select the appropriate Spot Fleet allocation strategy (lowestPrice, diversified, capacityOptimized, priceCapacityOptimized) for a workload.

notes: Focus pages 52-57 (security groups) and 64-77 (purchasing options) hardest: exam Task 1.2 and Task 4.2 are built on them. Distractor patterns to expect: connection timeout = security group vs 'connection refused' = app issue; Dedicated Host (placement control, BYOL per-socket/core) vs Dedicated Instance (no placement control, may share hardware within account); Capacity Reservations (no discount, paid whether used or not) vs Regional Reserved Instances/Savings Plans; Spot for resilient/flexible batch workloads, never critical databases. Source states discounts are illustrative only — AWS changes them, so reason from workload characteristics, not exact percentages. Page 45 and pages 58-63 are hands-on/lab material; only the port-22 and EC2 Instance Connect facts are exam-relevant.
